title: Virginia bans sale of geolocation data
summary: Virginia has enacted legislation that bans the sale of sensitive geolocation data as part of its Consumer Data Protection Act (CDPA), marking a significant expansion of consumer privacy rights in the state. The law requires explicit consent before collecting or sharing location data and imposes strict penalties for non-compliance.
problem_solved: Addresses the growing concern over unauthorized collection and commercialization of consumer location data by companies.
why_valuable: This legislation provides consumers with stronger privacy protections for their sensitive geolocation information and sets a precedent that may influence privacy legislation in other US states.
